newsitem.title: CANADA: Delgratia can't account for stock price.
newsitem.headline: Delgratia can't account for stock price.

text.p: Delgratia Mining Corp said on Friday it had no knowledge of any material facts that would account for the recent fluctuations in the price of its stock.
But the exploration company said it regretted media reports estimating the gold reserves at its 70 percent-owned Nevada project at five million ounces.
"I believe that it is premature to quantify the potential of this gold system," Charles Ager, president and chairman of Delgratia, said in a statement.
Delgratia was halted on Nasdaq today. The stock fell 17-5/8 to 16 on Thursday.
"I believe that it is premature to quantify the potential of this gold system. Current exploration programs for the Coco Mina and the Nevada projects are fully funded," Ager said.
Ager expressed confidence that there were major gold systems on each of its projects.
"It remains to be determined how big they each are. This will be demonstrated in fact by the exploration and drilling efforts currently underway," Ager added.
Delgratia is exploring on gold projects in Nicaragua, Mexico and Nevada. It plans to buy and explore properties it thinks could contain reserves of more than five million ounces.
The Coco Mina project in Nicaragua and the Nevada project in the United States both meet this criteria, Delgratia said.

"To date, there are proven resources of 1.7 million ounces gold equivalent (gold plus zinc) on the Coco Mina project and a field program is underway to expand these reserves. In Nevada, even though the first four holes of the drilling program are very encouraging, it is premature to quantify the potential of this gold system," Delgratia said.

Delgratia is conducting a 75,000 foot drilling program (75 holes averaging 1000 feet each) in Nevada designed to test the depth extent of gold mineralization outlined within a geochemical anomaly at the surface.

"The company is satisfied that these results demonstrate that gold mineralization has been found to occur within an oxidized sequence of sedimentary beds from the surface to depths of about 1000 feet," Delgratia said.
